title: Buildings With an Ocean View
statement: `n` buildings stand in a row, and the ocean lies past the right end of the row. `heights[i]` is the height of building `i` (indices start at 0). A building has an ocean view when every building to its right is strictly shorter than it, so an equal or taller building anywhere to its right blocks the view; the last building always has one. Return the indices of all buildings with an ocean view, sorted in increasing order.
notes:
## Intuition

Checking every building against all buildings to its right is O(n²). Instead, scan from left to right and keep a stack of the buildings that still have a view so far. When a new building arrives, every stacked building that is not taller than it has just lost its view for good, and those buildings are exactly the ones on top of the stack, because the stack's heights strictly decrease from bottom to top. Pop them, push the new one, and at the end the stack holds the answer already in increasing index order.

## Approach

1. Start with an empty `stack` of indices.
2. For each index `i`, pop while the building on top of `stack` has height `<= heights[i]`: building `i` blocks it.
3. Push `i`; nothing to its right has been seen yet, so it currently has a view.
4. Return `stack`.

## Example 1, step by step

For `heights = [4, 2, 3, 1]`: push `0` → `[0]`; height 2 is shorter than 4, push → `[0, 1]`; height 3 blocks building 1 (height 2), pop it and push → `[0, 2]`; height 1 is shorter than 3, push → `[0, 2, 3]`. The answer is `[0, 2, 3]`.

## Complexity

- Time: O(n): each index is pushed once and popped at most once.
- Space: O(n) for the stack, which is also the output.

## Pitfalls

- Equal heights block the view, so pop on `<=`, not just `<`.
- The last building always has a view; do not drop it.
- Return indices in increasing order; a right-to-left scan collects them backwards and needs a reverse.

## Variables

| Name | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `stack` | indices of buildings that still see the ocean, heights strictly falling from bottom to top |
| `i` | index of the building being added |

narration.2: The stack holds the indices that have a view among the buildings seen so far.
narration.3: Add buildings one at a time from left to right.
narration.4: The top building is not taller than building i, so i blocks its view.
narration.5: Remove it; it can never see the ocean now.
narration.7: Nothing stands to the right of building i yet, so it has a view for now.
narration.9: The survivors, in increasing index order, are the buildings with an ocean view.
